episodes.186863: Severe thunderstorms ahead of a cold front produced numerous marine thunderstorm wind gusts.
episodes.186877: Severe thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front and produced some hail and damage.
episodes.187660: A strong cold front impacted the Hawaiian Islands and brought periods of heavy rain and gusty winds. This resulted in flooding over portions of the islands as well as wind damage.
episodes.188236: Moisture rich air with near record precipitable water, for this time of year, surged north from the Gulf of Mexico across the local area as a warm front lifted northward. Increased lift from both the warm/moist airmass and front boundary primed the environment for robust updrafts. Mid and upper levels of the atmosphere began to cool as an upper level system approached the area. That combo of increasing instability and ample moisture resulted in a few severe storm over the local coastal waters.
episodes.188238: Moisture rich air with near record precipitable water, for this time of year, surged north from the Gulf of Mexico across the local area as a warm front lifted northward. Increased lift from both the warm/moist airmass and front boundary primed the environment for robust updrafts. Mid and upper levels of the atmosphere began to cool as an upper level system approached the area. That combo of of instability and ample moisture created an environment able to sustain a variety of severe weather ranging from a tornado to damaging winds and hail.
episodes.188320: Scattered thunderstorms developed across parts of East Texas in the early afternoon on January 8th, mainly along and north of a surface warm front oriented across Southeast Texas. Near and south of the front, surface dew points rose into the mid and upper 60s, with MLCAPE values of 2000-3000 J/kg. Wind profiles near the warm front showed very strong low-level vertical shear. Thunderstorms were initially elevated through the mid-morning hours with primarily a large hail threat, but daytime heating began to aid in additional convective development along the warm front by late morning into the early afternoon. This led to the development of surface-based thunderstorms with increasing potential for some damaging wind gusts, and one such storm produced very isolated wind damage in Sabine County Texas.
episodes.188399: A low pressure system moving east through the region brought severe thunderstorms, flash flooding, and strong gradient winds to portions of Mississippi.
episodes.188493: An area of low pressure developed over the Texas Hill Country and moved toward east Texas and western Louisiana. Severe weather occurred along a warm front and then a few more strong to severe storms developed with the cold front.
episodes.188494: An area of low pressure developed over the Texas Hill Country and moved toward east Texas. Severe weather occurred along a warm front and then a few more strong to severe storms developed with the cold front.
episodes.188590: Strong south to southeasterly low-level flow brought an unusually warm, moist airmass to South Central Texas ahead of a Pacific cold front. The front moved into an airmass with temperatures in the middle to upper 70s and dewpoints in the 60s. A few thunderstorms developed ahead of the front and some of these produced large hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.188605: A line of strong thunderstorms moved through the southern Coastal Bend south of San Patricio County. This led to a severe thunderstorm wind gust measured at KNGP ASOS on January 8th.

events.narrative: Two inch in diameter hail was observed at the National Weather Service office.
A thunderstorm wind gust ripped a large RV awning from the ground and carried it into power lines. A couple power poles were also downed and a nearby home had minor roof damage.
Two inch in diameter hail was observed from Downtown Lake Charles to Sowela Community College.
Quarter size hail reported through social media.
A wooden porch was lifted off of a home near the intersection of State Highway 103 and FM Road 1592. A tree was also downed along with damage to a concession stand and a nearby trampoline.
An off duty NWS employee observed flooding along Enterprise BLVD near Interstate 210. Flooding of other nearby streets also was reported.
A thunderstorm produced quarter size hail in Belmont.
A thunderstorm produced 2.25 inch diameter hail in Belmont.
A thunderstorm produced tennis ball size hail near the H-4 dam on Lake Gonzales.
A thunderstorm produced hail from two to three inches in diameter approximately six miles west of Gonzales. Pictures of the hail were posted on X.
A thunderstorm produced nickel size hail near Hwy 183 and I-10 southeast of Luling.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 70 mph that knocked down a traffic light at the intersection of St. Joseph St. and St. Lawrence St. in Gonzales.
A thunderstorm produced hail up to the size of tennis balls that dented a car in Gonzales. The average hail stones were golf ball size.
A thunderstorm produced golf ball size hail on Hwy 90 west of Gonzales.
A spotter reported a tornado near Coldspring. Further investigation into the report following the event did not yield any evidence of a tornado touchdown, but rather the formation of a funnel cloud.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 70 mph that downed a power line on St. Joseph St. in Gonzales.

A local news outlet reported a possible waterspout over Lake Livingston. Photographic evidence and investigations after the event did not show any evidence that a tornado touched down over land on either side of the Lake.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 70 mph that blew a tree onto a power line on Alt US Hwy 77 near the railroad crossing in Yoakum.
Broadcast media and local fire departments observed numerous streets flooded in Franklin. Some flooded with over 2 feet of water.
Pea to penny sized hail was observed on Highway 36 just south of Kenney.
Golf ball sized hail fell near Brooklyn.
Hail up to quarter sized was observed south of Rock Island.

An EF0 tornado with maximum winds of 80 MPH touched down at the intersection of Highway 1011 and Supreme Cross Road in Supreme, LA. The tornado tracked almost due north-northeast along Highway 1011 before curving slightly northwest at the end. This was confirmed via radar. The west side of the road sustained the heaviest damage, all to manufactured homes. Only one actual mobile home was flipped and thrown into the fire station. This was noted to be of very degraded construction with only one strap seen. None of the homes surveyed had a sustained load path with strapping. A few were pushed slightly off their foundations with roof damage and undercarriage damage. To the east of Highway1011, these were well-built homes with only tree damage and minor roof/gutter damage. We do believe the tornado was wide enough to cause damage on both sides but the construction was better on theeast side, hence the lower damage. Around the intersections of Highway 1, Highway 1011, and Highway 308, there were trees down, a few pieces of roof pulled off and damage to a thrift store. The|concrete blocks at the top were pushed off with significant roof damage. Throughout the track, debris was noted well away from where it came from, with the thrift store's roof both to the eastand to the west. Debris indentations in the ground were widely seen and debris splatter was noted on all sides of the buildings. Also to note, off to the east on Highway 1014, power poles were leaning in one direction with very minor siding damage to a few manufactured homes. This is well away from the track and the damage is either straight-line winds or inflow from the tornado.
Hail up to the size of half dollars fell in Yazoo City.
The Weatherflow mesonet at Bayou Bienvenue measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 49 knots or 57 mph.
A severe thunderstorm damaged or downed several trees and power lines in Colmesneil. One home also sustained minor roof damage.
Power lines downed in Batson.
Hail of quarter size or larger fell near Chatham and caused small dents to a car driving along MS Highway 1.
The Weatherflow mesonet at Mid Lake Pontchartrain measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 50 knots or 58 mph.
There was some damage to street signs, and a street light was downed and damaged.
A large tree was downed near the intersection on Mykawa Road and Bellfort Avenue.
Flash flooding was observed at Makaha Valley Towers. A video of flash flooding was seen |through social media. The flow of the flash flooding was moving down Kili Drive.
A thunderstorm wind gust of 57 knots or 66 mph was measured at the MSY International-Louis Armstrong Airport.
Trees downed by a passing storm north of Buna.
Trees and power lines were downed near the intersection of Fresa Road and Lafferty Road.
The Weatherflow mesonet at Mid Lake Pontchartrain measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 37 knots or 42 mph.
NWS Employee in Mandeville reported 1 inch sized hail.
Severe thunderstorm wind gusts knocked down some power lines near Bon Wier.
Wind gust occurred at the Texas Yacht Club WeatherFlow site (XTCY).
Wind gust occurred at the Palacios ASOS site (KPSX).
Wind gust occurred at the Galveston Bay WeatherFlow site (XGAL).
Flash flooding was reported along Windsor Boulevard in the River Forest Subdivision. Water covered many streets and some garages got water in them.
Heavy rainfall resulted in several inches of water over multiple locations along I-12 between Covington and Slidell.
ASOS at CC-NAS reported a 55 knot wind gust with the passing of strong thunderstorms.
Quarter sized hail was reported in Pearl River.
